name: – Ingeborg Ter Laak – Commission proposal
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council suspending the application of the rules on the appointment of an authorised representative for extended producer responsibility for batteries and waste batteries and packaging and packaging waste
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to pause a rule for small companies. Under current European Union law, a company selling batteries or packaging in another European Union country must appoint a local "authorised representative" there. The Parliament's position is to suspend that duty until 1 January 2035, or until a new wider European Union law on producer responsibility takes effect, whichever comes first. The pause would only cover micro and small companies based in the European Union.

- **What changes:** Micro and small European Union producers no longer need an authorised representative in each country where they sell.
- **Who it affects:** Small and micro firms selling batteries or packaging across borders; larger firms and non-European Union producers keep the duty.
- **What happens next:** Parliament's position goes to the Council of the European Union for negotiation before the law can be adopted.
